This appeal is by the claimant filed
under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, the Act') being aggrieved by the
judgment and award dated 30.12.2021 passed by the Ii Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and Mact,
Kalaburagi in Mvc No.6/2020 seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 29.10.2019 when deceased NC: 2025:KHC-K:6566-DB HC-KAR Umesh was proceeding on the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/EB-1220 towards Dudhani from Afzalpur, at about 4.15 p.m., when deceased approached near Bus- Depot on Afzalpur to Dudhani road, at that time, one KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-32/F-2148 came from opposite side from Dudhani side in high speed, rash and The Managing Director Nekrtc vs Parvati W/O Late Basanna Sakre on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144104775/
2 negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle.

Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his head, multiple fracture to brain and blood was oozing from the nose and ear and died on the spot.
3. Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month by doing Tailoring and Garments business.
The petitioner being mother of deceased has lost the earning member of the family due to untimely death of deceased.
Hence, the claimant filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Act before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6566-DB HC-KAR 4.
Pursuant to the summons, respondent appeared and filed statement of objections denying the entire claim petition averments and sought to dismiss the claim petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
In order to prove the case, claimant got examined herself as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely, Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

On behalf of respondent, three witnesses are examined as R.Ws.1 to 3 and got marked four document as Exs.R.1 to 4.
6.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment inter alia held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Bus, as a result of which,
deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal, upon considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, held that the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.18,35,800/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. NC: 2025:KHC-K:6566-DB HC-KAR and directed respondent - NEKRTC (for short, 'the Corporation') to deposit the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, the appellant - Corporation is in this appeal impugning the liability and as well as the quantum of compensation.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant raised the following contentions:
a) The learned counsel appearing for the Corporation has contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of deceased, who was riding the motorcycle on the wrong side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the driver of the KSRTC Bus alone is negligent in causing the accident.
b) The rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 41/EB-1220 came in a rash and negligent manner on the extreme right side of the road and dashed to the offending Bus.
Due to the impact, deceased fell down and sustained injuries and died on the spot.

sentences.text: To disprove the case of the claimant, the Corporation has examined the driver of the Bus as R.W.1.
In his evidence, he has categorically stated that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by deceased.
They have also produced the photographs marked at Ex.R.1.
The Tribunal without considering all these aspect of the matter has committed error in holding that the driver of the bus alone is negligent in causing the accident.

d) Lastly, in respect of quantum of compensation is concerned, it is submitted that considering the age and avocation of deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Hence, on these grounds prayed to allow the appeal.
8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the claimant/respondent has contended that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending bus.
Immediately after the accident, complaint has been NC: 2025:KHC-K:6566-DB HC-KAR lodged against the driver of the bus.
The Police after thorough investigation filed charge-sheet against the driver of the Bus.
The Tribunal after considering the IMV report at Ex.P.6 and evidence of the parties, has rightly held that driver of the Bus is alone negligent in causing the accident.
Hence, supporting the impugned judgment and award, sought to dismiss the appeal.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent, perused the judgment and award including the appeal papers.
10.

It is the case of the claimant that on 29.10.2019, deceased Umesh was proceeding towards Dudhani from Afzalpur on Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 41/EB-1220 at about 4.15 p.m. when deceased approached near Bus-Depot on Afzalpur to Dudhani road, at that time, one KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-32/F- 2148 came from opposite side from Dudhani side in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6566-DB HC-KAR motorcycle.

Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his head, multiple fracture to brain and blood was oozing from the nose and ear and died on the spot.
11.
To prove the case, the claimant has been examined herself as P.W.1.
She has reiterated entire averments made in the claim petition.
To disprove the case of the claimant, respondent has examined the driver of the Bus as R.W.1.
In his evidence, he has categorically stated that deceased was negligent in causing the accident.
After the complaint has been lodged, the concerned official has drawn IMV report.
From which, it is very clear that the front portion of the motorcycle has been damaged and left portions of the bus is damaged.

Considering the evidence of P.W.1, R.W.1, Ex.R.1 - Photographs and IMV report as per Ex.P.6, it is very clear that both rider of motorcycle i.e., deceased as well as driver of the offending Bus were negligent in causing the accident.

After having gone through the complaint, charge-sheet, evidence and IMV report, we are of the opinion that the rider of the motorcycle i.e., deceased has contributed negligence to the extent of 20% in causing the accident.
To that extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

14. In respect of quantum of compensation is concerned, considering the age and avocation of deceased, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and no interference is warranted.

15. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.

- 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6566-DB HC-KAR b) The judgment and award of the Claims Tribunal is modified to the extent; directing the respondent - Corporation to deposit 80% of the compensation amount along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
c) The amount deposited by the appellant - Corporation before this Court shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
